claims.text: Conventional pressureless sintering of single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 typically has a relatively porous, less-dense microstructure.
The porous microstructure of conventionally sintered ZrB2 is prone to surface attack during long-term exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Spark plasma sintering can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 2000 °C.
SPS at approximately 2000 °C can achieve full densification of ZrB2.
SPS processing will produce a finer and more homogeneous ZrB2 microstructure with significantly reduced residual porosity and grain-boundary defects.
SPS applies pulsed electric currents and uniaxial pressure during consolidation.
The pulsed currents and uniaxial pressure used in SPS promote rapid densification of ZrB2 at lower temperatures.
Rapid heating and short dwell time reduce the time available for grain growth and pore coarsening.
Reduced grain growth and pore coarsening result in a denser ZrB2 ceramic.
Greater ZrB2 density and lower porosity improve mechanical strength.
A denser ZrB2 microstructure acts as a barrier against plating-liquid penetration and subsequent defect propagation.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have higher flexural and compressive strength than conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will exhibit markedly less hole formation and related failure during prolonged liquid-plating exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Exposure at approximately 90 °C for 100 hours is proposed as the service boundary for comparing plating-bath resistance.
